chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Inform me about the Will, is it from Allah or from the creation?' He said: 'The will of the creation is the inner self (conscience), and what manifests from it afterwards in the form of action. As for Allah, the Mighty and High, His Will is His Creating (making), and nothing else, because He does not reflect, does not imagine, and does not think. These attributes are absent from Him, and they are attributes of the created beings. Thus, Allah’s Will is the Action itself, and nothing else. He says to it: “Be,” and it is, without a word or speech by the tongue, without imagination or thought, and without a “how” to it, just as He is without a “how.”'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between human will and Divine Will in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to articulate the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity, asserting that Allah’s Will is not a distinct attribute or internal deliberation but is identical to His essence and act of creation. This refutes anthropomorphic views by emphasizing that, unlike creatures who move from potentiality to actuality through thought, God’s command 'Be' (Kun) is immediate and devoid of temporal sequence or linguistic mediation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 17.Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (RA) said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Jabbar, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya that I enquired from Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim (AS): “Inform me about the Will. Is it a part of Allah or is it of the Creation? Hence, he (AS) answered, The will is part of the created conscience, and it manifest itself in action. As for Will of Allah, the Mighty and High, then it is His Making [ihdath] and none other than that because He does not reflect, does not imagine, and does not think. These attributes cannot be applied to Him as they are attributes of creation. Thus, Allah’s Will is action and nothing else. He says to it: “Be and it is,” without a word or speech expressed by tongue, by imagination or by thought. His Will is expressed without form in the same way that He is without form.
